title: Simple Machines
standard_code: Grade 6, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy
standard_text: Simple machines (lever, wheel and axle, pulley, inclined plane, wedge, screw) make work easier by changing the size or direction of a force. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 6, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy)
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy): pulleys, gears, levers and other machines, work and energy and mechanical advantage. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Simple machines change the size or direction of a force.
key_sub: Less force over a longer distance.
body_html:
How to think about it

The six simple machines are the lever, wedge, inclined plane, wheel and axle, pulley and screw. They make work easier by changing the size or direction of a force: a ramp lets you use less force over a longer distance.

Compound machines, like a bicycle, combine simple machines. Your arm is a natural lever. Power is how fast energy is transferred: a more powerful motor does the same work in less time.

Example

Which simple machine is a ramp?

A sloping surface

Answer: an inclined plane

Example

A single fixed pulley on a flagpole: what does it change?

You pull down, the flag goes up.

Answer: the direction of the force

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a machine reduces the work done (it reduces the force).
  • Mixing up a wedge and an inclined plane.
  • Thinking power and force are the same.

faq.q: Why is a door handle far from the hinges?
faq.a: A longer lever arm needs less force to turn the door.
The rate of transferring energy, measured in watts.

items.q: What happens when two gears touch and one turns?
c: The other turns the opposite way.
The other turns the same way.
items.e: Teeth push each other.

items.q: A 16-tooth gear drives a 48-tooth gear. The small gear turns 3 times. How many times does the big gear turn?
items.e: The big gear has 3 times as many teeth, so it turns 3 times more slowly. 3 ÷ 3 = 1.

items.q: To make a seesaw balance with a heavier child, where should the heavier child sit?
items.e: Moving closer reduces their turning effect.

items.q: What kind of mechanism is used in a well bucket on a rope?
items.e: Levers, pulleys and gears are simple machines.

items.q: A clock has many gears. Why?
c: so the hands turn at different speeds
items.e: Gears of different sizes turn at different speeds.

items.q: Two gears are meshed. The first turns clockwise. Which way does the second turn?
items.e: Meshed gears turn in opposite directions.

items.q: A 12-tooth gear drives a 48-tooth gear. The big gear turns 2 times. How many times does the small gear turn?
items.e: Each turn of the big gear moves 48 teeth, which is 4 turns of the small gear. 2 × 4 = 8.

items.q: Which machine part transfers turning motion from one shaft to another?
items.e: Gears pass turning motion along.

items.q: Why do people oil the gears of a bike?
c: to reduce friction so they turn easily
items.e: Less friction, less wear.

items.q: Which tool uses a pulley to lift heavy car engines in a garage?
items.e: Chain blocks use several pulleys.

items.q: Which simple machine is made of a rope over a grooved wheel?
items.e: That is the definition of a pulley.

items.q: What is a mechanism?
c: a device that makes a force have a bigger effect or changes its direction
items.e: Levers, pulleys and gears.

items.q: Which mechanism changes turning motion into up-and-down motion in a toy?
items.e: Cams are used in moving toys.

items.q: In a pulley system, why does the effort get smaller with more ropes?
c: The load is shared between the ropes.
items.e: But you pull more rope.

items.q: What kind of mechanism is used in window blinds?
items.e: Levers, pulleys and gears are simple machines.

items.q: Why is it easier to open a paint can with a long screwdriver than with a coin?
c: The longer lever needs less effort.
items.e: A longer lever arm means less effort.

items.q: Which machine changes a small turning force at the handle into a big force at the axle?
c: a wheel and axle, like a doorknob
items.e: The big wheel makes turning easier.

items.q: Why do some gear systems use a very big gear driven by a tiny gear?
c: to make the big gear turn with more force
to make the big gear spin faster
items.e: A slow big gear turns with more force.

items.q: A bike rider changes to a bigger back gear to climb a hill. What happens?
c: Pedaling is easier but the bike goes slower.
items.e: Gears trade speed for force.

items.q: How can you make a lever lift a load with less effort?
items.e: Longer distance, less force.

items.q: A small gear with 12 teeth drives a big gear with 36 teeth. How many times does the small gear turn while the big gear turns 1 time?
items.e: 36 ÷ 12 = 3 small turns for each big turn.

items.q: A small gear with 20 teeth drives a big gear with 40 teeth. How many times does the small gear turn while the big gear turns 3 times?
items.e: 40 ÷ 20 = 2 small turns for each big turn.

items.q: A 24-tooth gear drives a 96-tooth gear. The small gear turns 4 times. How many times does the big gear turn?
items.e: The big gear has 4 times as many teeth, so it turns 4 times more slowly. 4 ÷ 4 = 1.

items.q: A small gear with 12 teeth drives a big gear with 24 teeth. How many times does the small gear turn while the big gear turns 1 time?
items.e: 24 ÷ 12 = 2 small turns for each big turn.

items.q: A 10-tooth gear drives a 40-tooth gear. The big gear turns 1 time. How many times does the small gear turn?
items.e: Each turn of the big gear moves 40 teeth, which is 4 turns of the small gear. 1 × 4 = 4.

items.q: 5 gears are meshed in a row: A → B → C → D → E. Gear A turns counterclockwise. Which way does gear E turn?
items.e: Each meshed gear turns the opposite way to the one before it. With 5 gears, gear E turns counterclockwise.

items.q: A small gear with 12 teeth drives a big gear with 36 teeth. The small gear turns 6 times. How many times does the big gear turn?
Which pair of gears would turn the slowest output gear?
items.e: The bigger the driven gear compared with the driver, the slower it turns.

items.q: Gear A (12 teeth) turns clockwise and drives gear B (48 teeth). Which way does gear B turn?
items.e: Two gears that touch turn in opposite directions.

items.q: A small gear with 12 teeth drives a big gear with 36 teeth. How many times does the small gear turn while the big gear turns 6 times?
items.e: 36 ÷ 12 = 3 small turns for each big turn.

items.q: 3 gears are meshed in a row: A → B → C. Gear A turns clockwise. Which way does gear C turn?
items.e: Each meshed gear turns the opposite way to the one before it. With 3 gears, gear C turns clockwise.

items.q: A 16-tooth gear drives a 64-tooth gear. The small gear turns 4 times. How many times does the big gear turn?
items.e: The big gear has 4 times as many teeth, so it turns 4 times more slowly. 4 ÷ 4 = 1.

items.q: A small gear with 20 teeth drives a big gear with 40 teeth. How many times does the small gear turn while the big gear turns 2 times?
items.e: 40 ÷ 20 = 2 small turns for each big turn.

items.q: A small gear with 10 teeth drives a big gear with 40 teeth. How many times does the small gear turn while the big gear turns 2 times?
items.e: 40 ÷ 10 = 4 small turns for each big turn.

items.q: A 15-tooth gear drives a 60-tooth gear. The big gear turns 5 times. How many times does the small gear turn?
items.e: Each turn of the big gear moves 60 teeth, which is 4 turns of the small gear. 5 × 4 = 20.

items.q: 4 gears are meshed in a row: A → B → C → D. Gear A turns counterclockwise. Which way does gear D turn?
items.e: Each meshed gear turns the opposite way to the one before it. With 4 gears, gear D turns clockwise.

items.q: 2 gears are meshed in a row: A → B. Gear A turns clockwise. Which way does gear B turn?
items.e: Each meshed gear turns the opposite way to the one before it. With 2 gears, gear B turns counterclockwise.

items.q: 4 gears are meshed in a row: A → B → C → D. Gear A turns clockwise. Which way does gear D turn?
items.e: Each meshed gear turns the opposite way to the one before it. With 4 gears, gear D turns counterclockwise.

items.q: A 12-tooth gear drives a 48-tooth gear. The small gear turns 8 times. How many times does the big gear turn?
items.e: The big gear has 4 times as many teeth, so it turns 4 times more slowly. 8 ÷ 4 = 2.

items.q: A 20-tooth gear drives a 40-tooth gear. The big gear turns 5 times. How many times does the small gear turn?
items.e: Each turn of the big gear moves 40 teeth, which is 2 turns of the small gear. 5 × 2 = 10.

items.q: Why does an elevator use a motor and pulleys?
c: to lift heavy loads with less effort
items.e: Machines make work easier.

items.q: A 24-tooth gear drives a 96-tooth gear. The big gear turns 1 time. How many times does the small gear turn?
items.e: Each turn of the big gear moves 96 teeth, which is 4 turns of the small gear. 1 × 4 = 4.

items.q: A 30-tooth gear drives a 120-tooth gear. The small gear turns 12 times. How many times does the big gear turn?
items.e: The big gear has 4 times as many teeth, so it turns 4 times more slowly. 12 ÷ 4 = 3.

items.q: Which simple machine is a wheel with a rope that can be fixed or movable?
items.e: Pulleys can be fixed or movable.

items.q: What kind of mechanism is used in tweezers?
items.e: Levers, pulleys and gears are simple machines.

items.q: What does a single fixed pulley do?
c: It changes the direction of the force.
items.e: You pull down to lift up.

items.q: What kind of mechanism is used in a bicycle chain and sprockets?
items.e: Levers, pulleys and gears are simple machines.

items.q: What kind of mechanism is used in scissors?
items.e: Levers, pulleys and gears are simple machines.

items.q: Which design change would make a gear train turn its last gear faster?
items.e: A smaller driven gear turns faster.

items.q: A flag is raised by pulling down on a rope. Which machine is at the top of the pole?
items.e: A fixed pulley changes the direction of the force.

items.q: What is a pulley?
c: a flat board on a pivot
a wheel with a groove that a rope runs over
items.e: Pulleys help lift loads.

items.q: A 24-tooth gear drives a 96-tooth gear. The small gear turns 8 times. How many times does the big gear turn?
items.e: The big gear has 4 times as many teeth, so it turns 4 times more slowly. 8 ÷ 4 = 2.

items.q: A 30-tooth gear drives a 90-tooth gear. The small gear turns 6 times. How many times does the big gear turn?
items.e: The big gear has 3 times as many teeth, so it turns 3 times more slowly. 6 ÷ 3 = 2.

items.q: A pulley system makes lifting easier. What is the trade-off?
c: You have to pull more rope.
items.e: Machines trade force for distance.

items.q: Gear A has 20 teeth and gear B has 10 teeth. Gear A turns once. How many times does gear B turn?
What is friction's effect in a machine?
c: It slows moving parts and wastes some energy as heat.
items.e: Oil reduces friction.

items.q: What happens to the speed of a load lifted with many pulleys?
c: It rises more slowly because you pull more rope.
items.e: Force is reduced, distance is increased.

items.q: What is the effort in a pulley system?
items.e: Effort is the force that makes the machine work.

items.q: What kind of mechanism is used in a flagpole rope?
items.e: Levers, pulleys and gears are simple machines.

items.q: Why do cranes use several pulleys together?
c: so a smaller force can lift a heavy load
items.e: More pulleys share the load, but you pull more rope.

items.q: A lever lifts a load of 160 N with an effort of 20 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
items.e: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = 160 ÷ 20 = 8.

items.q: A student pushes a box with a force of 50 N for 4 m. How much work is done?
items.e: Work = force × distance = 50 N × 4 m = 200 J.

items.q: A lever lifts a load of 125 N with an effort of 25 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
items.e: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = 125 ÷ 25 = 5.

items.q: What is the output of a system?
items.e: Forward motion is the output of a bike.

items.q: A light bulb receives 120 J of electrical energy and gives out 10 J of light energy. How much energy is converted to thermal energy?
items.e: Total energy out = total energy in: 120 − 10 = 110 J.

items.q: A student pushes a box with a force of 80 N for 2 m. How much work is done?
items.e: Work = force × distance = 80 N × 2 m = 160 J.

items.q: Kenneth does 800 J of work moving a load with a force of 200 N. How far does the load move?
items.e: distance = work ÷ force = 800 ÷ 200.

items.q: Mark pulls a sledge with a force of 40 N for 1.5 m. How much work is done?
items.e: work done = force × distance = 40 × 1.5 = 60 J.

items.q: A student pushes a box with a force of 30 N for 4 m. How much work is done?
items.e: Work = force × distance = 30 N × 4 m = 120 J.

items.q: Christian lifts a crate with a force of 150 N for 10 m. How much work is done?
items.e: work done = force × distance = 150 × 10 = 1,500 J.

items.q: Dennis pushes a box with a force of 20 N for 2 m. How much work is done?
items.e: work done = force × distance = 20 × 2 = 40 J.

items.q: A student pushes a box with a force of 40 N for 10 m. How much work is done?
items.e: Work = force × distance = 40 N × 10 m = 400 J.

items.q: What is a system?
c: a group of parts that work together to do a job
items.e: A bicycle is a mechanical system.

items.q: A lever lifts a load of 75 N with an effort of 25 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
items.e: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = 75 ÷ 25 = 3.

items.q: A light bulb receives 80 J of electrical energy and gives out 20 J of light energy. How much energy is converted to thermal energy?
items.e: Total energy out = total energy in: 80 − 20 = 60 J.

items.q: A lever lifts a load of 80 N with an effort of 20 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
items.e: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = 80 ÷ 20 = 4.

items.q: Kevin does 75 J of work moving a load with a force of 150 N. How far does the load move?
items.e: distance = work ÷ force = 75 ÷ 150.

items.q: A ball dropped with 200 J of potential energy bounces back up with 150 J. Where did the rest of the energy go?
c: It was stored in the ground forever as potential energy.
It became new mass in the ball.
It was converted to thermal and sound energy.
items.e: Energy is not destroyed: 50 J is converted to thermal and sound energy.

items.q: How can the efficiency of a bike be improved?
c: oil the chain and pump up the tires
items.e: Less friction, more useful output.

items.q: A machine uses 500 J of energy (work in) and does 300 J of useful work (work out). What is its efficiency?
items.e: Efficiency = work out ÷ work in × 100% = 300 ÷ 500 × 100% = 60%.

items.q: A lever lifts a load of 500 N with an effort of 100 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
items.e: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = 500 ÷ 100 = 5.

items.q: A lever lifts a load of 100 N with an effort of 50 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
items.e: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = 100 ÷ 50 = 2.

items.q: A lever lifts a load of 150 N with an effort of 50 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
items.e: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = 150 ÷ 50 = 3.

items.q: What is the unit of work and energy?
A machine uses 500 J of energy (work in) and does 125 J of useful work (work out). What is its efficiency?
items.e: Efficiency = work out ÷ work in × 100% = 125 ÷ 500 × 100% = 25%.

items.q: What is mechanical advantage?
c: how many times a machine multiplies the input force
items.e: MA = load ÷ effort.

items.q: A machine uses 800 J of energy (work in) and does 600 J of useful work (work out). What is its efficiency?
items.e: Efficiency = work out ÷ work in × 100% = 600 ÷ 800 × 100% = 75%.

items.q: A machine uses 400 J of energy (work in) and does 240 J of useful work (work out). What is its efficiency?
items.e: Efficiency = work out ÷ work in × 100% = 240 ÷ 400 × 100% = 60%.

items.q: Nico (weight 600 N) sits 2 m from the pivot of a see-saw. Rose weighs 500 N. How far from the pivot on the other side must Rose sit to balance it?
items.e: Balanced: 600 × 2 = 500 × d, so d = 2.4 m. The lighter person sits further away.

items.q: A force of 40 N is applied to a spanner 0.5 m from the pivot. What is the moment?
items.e: moment = force × distance from pivot = 40 × 0.5.

items.q: Which simple machine is a screw?
items.e: A screw is an inclined plane wrapped around a cylinder.

items.q: A student pushes a box with a force of 60 N for 2 m. How much work is done?
items.e: Work = force × distance = 60 N × 2 m = 120 J.

items.q: Kristine (weight 450 N) sits 1 m from the pivot of a see-saw. Rose weighs 300 N. How far from the pivot on the other side must Rose sit to balance it?
items.e: Balanced: 450 × 1 = 300 × d, so d = 1.5 m. The lighter person sits further away.

items.q: A student pushes a box with a force of 30 N for 3 m. How much work is done?
items.e: Work = force × distance = 30 N × 3 m = 90 J.

items.q: A lever lifts a load of 80 N with an effort of 40 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
items.e: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = 80 ÷ 40 = 2.

items.q: A lever lifts a load of 400 N with an effort of 100 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
items.e: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = 400 ÷ 100 = 4.

items.q: A force of 60 N is applied to a wheelbarrow handle 0.2 m from the pivot. What is the moment?
items.e: moment = force × distance from pivot = 60 × 0.2.

items.q: What is efficiency?
c: the percentage of input energy that becomes useful output
items.e: No machine is 100% efficient.

items.q: Why do ramps make it easier to move a wheelchair up a step?
c: A longer slope means less force is needed (but over a longer distance).
items.e: Inclined planes trade distance for force.

items.q: A lever lifts a load of 200 N with an effort of 50 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
items.e: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = 200 ÷ 50 = 4.
